name: Question 10
problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨3,\,3t,\,{t}^{3}⟩$ for $t>0,$ use the cross product curvature formula to find the curvature as a function of $t.$
worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(t)$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})⟩=⟨0,\,3,\,3{t}^{2}⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(3)^{2}+(3{t}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9+9{t}^{4}} \\  & =\sqrt{9(1+{t}^{4})} \\  & =3\sqrt{1+{t}^{4}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the second derivative ${r}^{″}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2})⟩=⟨0,\,0,\,6t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the cross-product:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t) & =⟨0,\,3,\,3{t}^{2}⟩\times ⟨0,\,0,\,6t⟩ \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 3 & 3{t}^{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 6t\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 3{t}^{2} \\ 0 & 6t\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}0 & 3{t}^{2} \\ 0 & 6t\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|k \\  & =18t\,i\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the magnitude of the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖ & =|18t|=18t.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that since $t>0$, we have $|t|=t.$
Therefore, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}=\frac{18t}{{(3\sqrt{1+{t}^{4}})}^{3}}=\frac{2t}{3(1+{t}^{4})^{3/2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Given the curve r(t)=⟨3,3t,t3⟩ for t>0, use the cross product curvature formula to find the curvature as a function of t.

a
3t4(1+t4)3/2
b
1(1+t4)3/2
c
t1+t4
d
231+t4
e
2t3(1+t4)3/2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The curvature κ(t) is given by

κ(t)=‖r′(t)×r″(t)‖‖r′(t)‖3.

First, we calculate r′(t) and ‖r′(t)‖:

r′(t)=⟨ddt(3),ddt(3t),ddt(t3)⟩=⟨0,3,3t2⟩‖r′(t)‖=02+(3)2+(3t2)2=9+9t4=9(1+t4)=31+t4

Next, we find the second derivative r″(t): r″(t)=⟨ddt(0),ddt(3),ddt(3t2)⟩=⟨0,0,6t⟩

Now, we compute the cross-product:

r′(t)×r″(t)=⟨0,3,3t2⟩×⟨0,0,6t⟩=|ijk033t2006t|=|33t206t|i−|03t206t|j+|0300|k=18ti

Then, we compute the magnitude of the above:

‖r′(t)×r″(t)‖=|18t|=18t.

Notice that since t>0, we have |t|=t. Therefore, the curvature is

κ(t)=‖r′(t)×r″(t)‖‖r′(t)‖3=18t(31+t4)3=2t3(1+t4)3/2.
